title: KV cache quantization sweep — INT8 vs FP8 evaluation and calibration
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Run a structured sweep and calibration validation for quantizing the KV cache (key/value tensors) across INT8 and FP8 formats. Goal: measure latency, memory, and generation-quality trade-offs for production LLMs (gpt-like and llama-family) across representative sequence lengths and request patterns. Deliverables: calibration recipes, a validated accuracy delta matrix vs baseline FP16, performance deltas (p50/p95 latency and throughput), and guidance for shipping KV-quantized profiles in runtime-2.4.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibration workflow reproducible in CI with documented steps. 2) For each tested model, a matrix of INT8/FP8 KV vs FP16 showing p50/p95 token latency, peak GPU memory, throughput, and quality delta (LM Eval or prompt-suite). 3) Decision doc recommending which KV quant profiles to promote to 'canary' and which require more work. 4) Bench harness PR merged and dashboard links created.
experiment_protocol: - Models: rm-7b-v2, open-llama-13b, gptx-8k-smoke. - Quant targets: INT8 asymmetric calibration, FP8 E4M3 and E5M2 (where supported). - KV-only quantization (weights for key/value projection and cached KV arrays), not full-MLP/attn quant. - Calibration datasets: 6 prompt families (QA, dialogue, long context summarization, code, instructions, multilingual). Use 500 samples per family for calibration; 2k held-out samples for validation. - Metrics: s/B (seconds per token), p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, peak GPU mem (MiB), ROUGE/EM for QA, and LM-eval perplexity when applicable. - Runs: baseline FP16 -> FP8 KV -> INT8 KV -> mixed fallback variants. - Each cell repeated 3x; record mean and std. - CI: integrate minimal run in perf-matrix nightly job.
calibration_workflow: 1) Offline histogram-collection pass using representative inputs to collect distribution for KV tensors. 2) Per-layer symmetric/asymmetric calibration analysis with outlier clipping heuristics. 3) Automated quant param search (grid: scale clipping at 99.9/99.5/99/98 percentiles) and choose param minimizing KL-divergence vs float32 activations. 4) Small synthetic replay to validate generation stability; store calibration artifacts (scale tensors) in artifact bucket. 5) Post-calibration accuracy sweep against held-out prompts to estimate degradation and tune per-layer exceptions.
experiment_results:
Summary of representative results (median over 3 runs):
- rm-7b-v2 (seq=2048): FP16 baseline p50=18ms, p95=55ms, peak GPU mem=9.6GB. FP8-KV p50=15.5ms (-14%), p95=48ms (-13%), mem=8.1GB (-15%), quality delta: +0.8% perplexity (negligible). INT8-KV p50=14.2ms (-21%), p95=42ms (-24%), mem=6.9GB (-28%), quality delta: +2.7% perplexity (small but measurable on multi-turn dialogue).
- open-llama-13b (seq=1024): FP16 p50=32ms, p95=110ms, mem=17.8GB. FP8-KV p50=27ms (-16%), p95=92ms (-16%), mem=15.0GB (-16%), quality delta: +1.1% EM drop on QA tasks. INT8-KV p50=24ms (-25%), p95=83ms (-25%), mem=13.2GB (-26%), quality delta: +4.9% EM drop (noticeable regressions on instruction-following and rare-token recall).
- gptx-8k-smoke (long-context): FP16 baseline p50=48ms, p95=160ms, mem=32.1GB. FP8-KV showed best trade-off (p50 -18%, mem -14%) with quality delta within 1.5%; INT8-KV had larger mem wins (-30%) but p95 regressions and higher variance.
Notes: INT8 KV gives larger memory savings and latency wins but introduces more frequent edge-case failures on rare-token generation and multi-turn stateful tests. FP8 is a safer default for canary. Full numbers and CSVs are attached in artifacts.
comments: 2026-03-02 Marcus Li: Initial histogram collection script committed to tmp branch; observed heavy-tailed distributions on keys for code prompts — included outlier-clipping in protocol.

2026-03-04 Elena Ruiz: Ran INT8 asymmetric vs symmetric calibration. Asymmetric helped for tokens with heavy long-tail counts but increased variance in some layers. Marking symmetric+outlier clip as default to reduce noise.
2026-03-07 Tom Barlow: Kernel selection needed a micro-optim for INT8 KV paths; patched GEMM runner in runtime and saw 6-8% extra token/sec on synthetic bench (PR #3471).

2026-03-10 Priya Kapoor: Validation sweep flagged reproducible EM drops on open-llama-13b INT8-KV on 'historical facts' prompts. Created follow-up ENG-6178 to investigate per-layer rollback heuristics.

2026-03-13 Marcus Li: Canary recommendation drafted: promote FP8-KV for rm-7b-v2 and gptx-8k-smoke with telemetry guards; hold INT8-KV behind experimental flag and per-customer opt-in due to higher QA regressions.
2026-03-14 Product review (Anna Meyer): Agreed with conservative rollout; asked for clear telemetry thresholds to auto-fallback on quality regressions (ENG-6190 created).
next_steps: 1) Finish CI integration: add one small-scale regression gate for FP8-KV in perf-matrix (ENG-6099 dependency). 2) Implement per-layer exception list and a fallback policy that reverts KV quant at inference-time if telemetry breach detected. 3) Ship FP8-KV 'canary' profiles for rm-7b-v2 and gptx-longcontext in runtime-2.4; document in release notes. 4) Continue INT8 work behind feature flag and expand calibration to cover multilingual rare-token distributions.
notes: Trade-offs: INT8 KV gives largest cost wins (memory and latency) but requires stricter calibration and per-layer exceptions to avoid tail-case quality regressions. FP8-KV is more robust and quicker to roll out. We should surface per-request quality telemetry (ROUGE/QA EM proxies) at SDK level to drive auto-fallback decisions.
